record.what_it_does: Visual discovery platform; API for pins, boards, ads, analytics, and conversions.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with scopes and refresh tokens. Redirect URIs must exactly match registered ones. The app ID and secret are issued after Pinterest approves the app. I did not confirm whether other methods exist, such as client credentials or conversion-API tokens.
record.access_notes: Free, but Pinterest reviews each app request before issuing credentials. Approved apps get Trial access: 1,000 requests/day, and Pins and Boards are visible only to their creator (sandbox-like). Standard access, needed to serve real users, requires an upgrade request. Community reports say this needs a video demo of the OAuth flow, with no published turnaround and some rejections. No paid plan was found.
record.api_breadth_notes: API v5 covers pins, boards, user account, media, search, ad accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, audiences, catalogs, conversion events, analytics and keywords. I did not count operations, but it is clearly over 50.
record.mcp_notes: developers.pinterest.com/about-pinterest-mcp/ lists https://api.pinterest.com/mcp (http transport, bearer token, OAuth 2.0). The page reads as a pre-launch announcement with a sign-up for updates, so general availability is unconfirmed. There are also many community and third-party MCP servers.
record.blocker_notes: Pinterest must approve the app for Trial access. Production use by other users needs a Standard upgrade, which requires review. Trial is limited to 1,000 requests/day, with content visible only to its creator.

evidence.quote: If approved for API use, your app receives Trial access, which is best for exploring our API features.
If you want to offer Pinterest capabilities to your users, we recommend upgrading to Standard access
Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest.
Be the first to know when it launches.
